newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Arbitrage play pulls down Philippine peso at close.
newsitem.headline: Arbitrage play pulls down Philippine peso at close.

text.p: * Central Bank sets selling rate at 26.375 to dollar
The Philippine peso ended weaker on Friday at 26.373 to the dollar as banks took advantage of the swap points during the long weekend, traders said.
The peso closed at 26.368 on Thursday.
The financial markets will be closed on Monday for nationwide local district elections. Trading will resume on Tuesday.
As a result, banks bought dollars for delivery Tuesday as well as earned the relatively higher peso interest rate during the three-day weekend.
"It's all part of the arbitrage play. Aside from that, there's no other factor which affected the market today," one trader said.
The peso fluctuated between 26.375 and 26.364, which was the selling price for dollars valued Friday.
The market was relatively quiet with only $131 million changing hands among banks. The Central Bank was seen selling dollars at 26.375 earlier in the day.
She said she expected the peso to firm up on Tuesday due to lack of dollar demand.
